name: pcap-viewer
description: Wireshark-like packet capture viewer for VS Code, powered by tshark.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode, the Python and tshark paths and the Lua dissectors come from your user settings only, so a workspace can't make PCAP Viewer run its own programs or scripts.

virtualWorkspaces.description: tshark reads files from disk: captures in a virtual workspace open as copies.

pcapViewer.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Python 3.14+ interpreter used to run the backend. Empty: try `python3.14`, `python3`, `python` (or `py -3.14` / `py -3` on Windows) from `PATH`.

pcapViewer.tsharkPath.markdownDescription: Path to `tshark`. Empty: search `PATH` and the default Wireshark install locations.

pcapViewer.luaScripts.markdownDescription: Lua dissector scripts passed to tshark as `-X lua_script:<path>`. Relative paths resolve against the first workspace folder.

pcapViewer.dissectorsFolder.markdownDescription: Folder whose `*.lua` files are loaded as dissectors in addition to `#pcapViewer.luaScripts#`. Relative paths resolve against the first workspace folder.

pcapViewer.decodeAs.markdownDescription: "Decode As" rules passed to tshark as `-d`, e.g. `tcp.port==8080,http`.

pcapViewer.prefs.markdownDescription: Wireshark preference overrides passed as `-o <name>:<value>`, e.g. `{ "tcp.desegment_tcp_streams": false }`.

pcapViewer.nameResolution.mac.markdownDescription: Show names for MAC addresses in the packet list and details: vendor prefixes and well-known addresses (`Broadcast`, `Dell_12:34:56`). Set with **PCAP: Name Resolution…** or the *Names* link in the viewer's status bar; a change re-indexes the captures it applies to (saved indexes make switching back instant).

pcapViewer.nameResolution.network.markdownDescription: Show host names for IP addresses. Names come from the capture's own DNS answers (`#pcapViewer.nameResolution.capturedDns#`), the system's hosts file and a `hosts` file in Wireshark's personal configuration folder; nothing is looked up unless `#pcapViewer.nameResolution.external#` is on. Cell filters and statistics keep using the addresses.

pcapViewer.nameResolution.capturedDns.markdownDescription: With `#pcapViewer.nameResolution.network#`, use the names learned from DNS responses in the capture (packets after the response show the name).

pcapViewer.nameResolution.transport.markdownDescription: Show service names for TCP/UDP/SCTP ports, e.g. `http(80)` in the Info column and the details.

pcapViewer.nameResolution.external.markdownDescription: With `#pcapViewer.nameResolution.network#`, also ask your DNS server for the names of the capture's addresses. It sends a query per address (the server sees them) and makes opening and filtering slower. A workspace can't turn this on.

pcapViewer.tlsKeyLogFile.markdownDescription: Key log file (the `SSLKEYLOGFILE` format browsers and curl write) used to decrypt TLS and QUIC traffic; passed to tshark as the `tls.keylog_file` preference (it overrides one in `#pcapViewer.prefs#`). Relative paths resolve against the capture's workspace folder. Set it with **PCAP: Set TLS Key Log File…**; changing it reloads the captures it applies to, and the viewer offers a reload when the file changes.

pcapViewer.columns.markdownDescription: Extra packet-list columns: any tshark field (e.g. `tcp.stream`, `http.host`) or `{ "field": "http.host", "title": "Host" }`.

order.description: Column ids in display order (number, time, source, destination, protocol, length, info, custom:<field>)

pcapViewer.columnLayout.markdownDescription: Packet list column order and hidden columns, by column id (`number`, `time`, `source`, `destination`, `protocol`, `length`, `info`, `custom:<field>`). Set by dragging headers and the header context menu.

enumDescriptions: Seconds since beginning of capture (or since the time reference)
Seconds since previous displayed packet (follows the filter and sort order)
Date and time of day, local time
Date and time of day, UTC
pcapViewer.timeFormat.markdownDescription: How the packet list shows the Time column (*PCAP: Time Display Format…*, or click the time format in the status bar).

pcapViewer.savedFilters.markdownDescription: Named display filters, e.g. `{ "name": "Web", "filter": "http || tls" }`. Shown in the filter bar's ★ menu and *PCAP: Saved Display Filters*. Set in user settings for all captures or in workspace settings to share with a project.

pcapViewer.filterButtons.markdownDescription: Buttons under the viewer's filter bar that apply a display filter in one click, like Wireshark's filter buttons, e.g. `{ "label": "DNS errors", "filter": "dns.flags.rcode != 0", "comment": "Failed lookups" }`. Add them with *PCAP: Add Filter Button…* or the bar's **+**; right-click a button to edit, move or remove it. Set in user settings for all captures or in workspace settings to share with a project.

pcapViewer.colorize.markdownDescription: Color the packet list with `#pcapViewer.coloringRules#` (*PCAP: Toggle Packet Coloring*).

default.name: Routing
default.filter: hsrp || eigrp || ospf || bgp || cdp || vrrp || carp || gvrp || igmp || ismp

pcapViewer.coloringRules.markdownDescription: Packet list coloring rules, like Wireshark's *View › Coloring Rules*: the **first** rule whose display filter matches colors the packet. Colors are `#rrggbb`; set `"enabled": false` to keep a rule without using it. *Colorize with Filter…* in the detail tree's context menu adds a rule at the top.

pcapViewer.maxCachedFrames.markdownDescription: Budget (in frame numbers) for cached filter results and sort orders in the backend. Each entry costs 4 bytes.

pcapViewer.capture.stopAfterPackets.markdownDescription: Stop a live capture (**PCAP: Start Capture…**) after this many packets. `0`: no limit.

pcapViewer.capture.stopAfterSeconds.markdownDescription: Stop a live capture after this many seconds. `0`: no limit.

pcapViewer.capture.stopAfterMegabytes.markdownDescription: Stop a live capture once its file reaches this size (MB). `0`: no limit. Until it is saved, the capture is kept in the extension's storage.

pcapViewer.capture.promiscuous.markdownDescription: Capture in promiscuous mode: also packets not addressed to this computer (on networks where they reach it).

pcapViewer.indexCache.enabled.markdownDescription: Save each capture's packet-list index (the result of the first tshark pass over the file) in the extension's storage, so reopening it is instant as long as the file and everything that changes dissection (tshark version, Lua scripts, Decode As rules, preferences, custom columns, your Wireshark configuration) are unchanged. The index holds the packet list's text (addresses, Info column). *PCAP: Clear Index Cache* deletes them all.

pcapViewer.indexCache.maxSizeMB.markdownDescription: Most disk space (MB) the saved indexes of `#pcapViewer.indexCache.enabled#` may use; the least recently opened captures' indexes go first. An index takes about 120 MB per million packets.

pcapViewer.quickDetail.after.markdownDescription: Showing a packet's details dissects the capture from the start up to that packet, so late packets in big captures take long (seconds per 100,000 packets). From this frame number on, a quick view comes first: only the `#pcapViewer.quickDetail.window#` packets before it are dissected (cut out with editcap), then the exact view replaces it. The quick view is marked approximate: reassembly, TCP analysis and conversation details that depend on earlier packets can be missing. `0` turns it off.

pcapViewer.quickDetail.window.markdownDescription: How many packets (up to and including the selected one) the quick view of `#pcapViewer.quickDetail.after#` dissects. More packets give more context (e.g. longer TCP reassembly) and take a little longer.

pcapViewer.requestTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Timeout for quick backend requests (packet detail, validation). Long operations (open, filter, sort) are not timed out but can be cancelled.

pcapViewer.ai.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer AI help through VS Code's Language Model API (GitHub Copilot): display filters (the filter bar's ✨ action, *PCAP: Suggest Display Filter…* and `@pcap` in chat), where only your request, the current filter and protocol/field names are sent and suggestions are checked with tshark; the capture summary (`@pcap /summary`), anomaly explanations (*Ask Copilot…* in the Expert Information and TCP Stream Graph panels, `@pcap /anomaly`) and `@pcap` questions answered with tools, which send statistics only if `#pcapViewer.ai.allowCaptureStatistics#` allows it; and explaining packets (*Ask Copilot About This Packet…*, `@pcap /explain`), which sends packet data only if `#pcapViewer.ai.allowPacketData#` allows it.

pcapViewer.ai.allowPacketData.markdownDescription: Allow *Ask Copilot About This Packet…* and `@pcap /explain` to send packet data to the language model: for at most 8 packets at a time, their packet-list row and dissection tree (field names and values, at most 250 lines each), plus your question and the current display filter. Raw bytes are not sent unless `#pcapViewer.ai.allowPacketBytes#` is also on. You are asked once when this is off. User settings only.

pcapViewer.ai.allowPacketBytes.markdownDescription: When explaining packets (with `#pcapViewer.ai.allowPacketData#`), also send raw bytes: the first 256 bytes of each packet as hex, and payload fields as bytes. Off: the hex dump is never sent and payload bytes are replaced by "[N bytes not sent]". User settings only.

pcapViewer.ai.allowCaptureStatistics.markdownDescription: Allow the AI features that send statistics computed from the capture (never packet contents) to the language model: *PCAP: Summarize Capture with Copilot* / `@pcap /summary`, *Ask Copilot…* in the Expert Information and TCP Stream Graph panels / `@pcap /anomaly`, and `@pcap` questions answered with tools. They send the capture properties, protocol hierarchy, top 15 conversations and endpoints (addresses, ports, host names, counts), expert information counts, traffic over time, the selected expert entries or up to 200 packets of a TCP stream as numbers and flags, and tool results (counts and statistics). You are asked once when this is off; `#pcapViewer.ai.allowPacketData#` implies it. User settings only.

chatParticipants.name: pcap
chatParticipants.description: Ask about the open capture (answered with tools where VS Code has them) or for a display filter; /summary, /anomaly, /explain

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain packets of the open capture, e.g. /explain 12 15-17 why the reset? (sends packet data: pcapViewer.ai.allowPacketData)

commands.name: summary
commands.description: Summarize the open capture from its statistics (sends statistics: pcapViewer.ai.allowCaptureStatistics)

commands.name: anomaly
commands.description: Explain expert information or a TCP stream, e.g. /anomaly stream 3 why so slow? (sends statistics: pcapViewer.ai.allowCaptureStatistics)

languageModelTools.name: pcap_capture_info
languageModelTools.userDescription: The open capture's packets, duration, size and link type (PCAP Viewer)
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Properties of the capture open in PCAP Viewer: number of packets, first/last packet time, duration, file size, link type and file format.

languageModelTools.name: pcap_count
languageModelTools.userDescription: Count the packets of the open capture matching a display filter (PCAP Viewer)
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Count the packets of the open capture that match a Wireshark display filter (for example 'dns.flags.rcode != 0' for failed DNS responses). Returns the match count and the total. Doesn't change what the viewer shows.

filter.description: A Wireshark display filter; empty counts every packet.

languageModelTools.name: pcap_stats
languageModelTools.userDescription: Protocol hierarchy, conversations, endpoints, expert information or IO statistics of the open capture (PCAP Viewer)
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Statistics of the open capture computed by tshark: 'phs' protocol hierarchy, 'conv' conversations or 'endpoints' (with type eth, ip, ipv6, tcp or udp; top rows by bytes), 'expert' expert information counts, 'io' packets and bytes over time. An optional display filter limits them to matching packets.

languageModelTools.name: pcap_field_search
languageModelTools.userDescription: Wireshark display filter fields by prefix (PCAP Viewer)
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find Wireshark display filter field names by prefix (for example 'dns.flags' or 'tcp.analysis'), with their types and descriptions. Use it before writing a filter with a field you are not sure about.

prefix.description: Start of a field or protocol name.

languageModelTools.name: pcap_list_packets
languageModelTools.userDescription: The first packets of the open capture matching a display filter, summary lines only (PCAP Viewer)
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the first packets of the open capture matching a display filter (at most 20): number, time, source, destination, protocol, length and info column only. Doesn't change what the viewer shows.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with PCAP Viewer
walkthroughs.description: Set up Python and TShark, open a capture, and find your way around the viewer.

steps.title: Install Python 3.14
steps.description:
The viewer's backend is a small Python program (standard library only). It needs Python 3.14 or newer.
[Check Again](command:pcapViewer.checkEnvironment)
Installed somewhere else? [Set the Python path](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22pcapViewer.pythonPath%22%5D).

steps.title: Install TShark
steps.description:
TShark, Wireshark's command-line dissector, reads the captures. It comes with Wireshark.
[Check Again](command:pcapViewer.checkEnvironment)
Installed somewhere else? [Set the TShark path](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22pcapViewer.tsharkPath%22%5D).

steps.title: Open a capture
steps.description:
Open any .pcap or .pcapng file from the Explorer, or try the sample capture.
[Open Sample Capture](command:pcapViewer.openSample)

steps.title: Filter packets
steps.description:
Type a display filter such as dns or tcp.port == 443 in the filter bar above the packet list. Fields are completed as you type.
[Apply a Display Filter](command:pcapViewer.applyFilter)

steps.title: Follow streams and see statistics
steps.description:
Follow a TCP stream from a packet's menu, or open the statistics: conversations, endpoints, protocol hierarchy, I/O graph and more.
[Show Conversations](command:pcapViewer.statistics.conversations)

steps.title: Ask Copilot (optional)
steps.description:
With GitHub Copilot, get display filters from a description, summaries of a capture and explanations of anomalies. Nothing from your capture is sent until you allow it.
[Review AI Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22pcapViewer.ai%22%5D)
